Build Architecture — what builds what, and what links where

The CMake target graph of this port: two projects, one handoff, and an FSP module registry added to upstream TF-M's target graph.

Every edge below was read out of a target_link_libraries() or target_sources() call and is cited by file and line. Unqualified port line numbers are platform/ext/target/renesas/ra6m5/CMakeLists.txt at TF-M HEAD after the D129 comment pass. A comment edit anywhere above a block moves them, so check the construct, not just the number. Upstream paths are relative to the trusted-firmware-m root.

ra8m2 has the same targets, not the same layout. It adds bl2 sources in three blocks (:843, :854, :858) where ra6m5 uses two, and its line numbers differ throughout — tfm_spm is :648 there against :517 here. The §3 table carries both columns; follow the construct into ra8m2/CMakeLists.txt rather than the ra6m5 line.

DESIGN.md says why the port is built this way — §1 (consume RASC, don't fork) and §1.1 (the documented deviations). This file says what the graph is.

1. Two projects, not one

The secure and non-secure sides are separate CMake projects. The first installs an api_ns/ tree; the second is configured against that tree, not against TF-M's source.

  • CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to <build dir>/api_ns — config/config_base.cmake:17.
  • api_ns/ carries interface/{include,src,lib}, image_signing/ and cmake/toolchain_ns_GNUARM.cmake.
  • The NS project needs both CONFIG_SPE_PATH and TFM_TOOLCHAIN_FILE pointing into it.

The -S source differs by what you are building. Regression (reg_build_gcc.bat:150,174) configures the SPE from tf-m-tests/tests_reg/spe and the NS project from tf-m-tests/tests_reg. Application (app_build_ra8m2_gcc.bat:50,69) configures the SPE from the TF-M root and the NS project from platform/ext/target/renesas/<part>/ns_app. Everything else below is identical; the diagram shows the regression flow.

e2 studio solution            SPE project                     NS project
(inputs; never built          cmake -S tests_reg/spe          cmake -S tests_reg
 by CMake)                    (regression; the app build      (regression; the app build
                               uses the TF-M root)             uses <part>/ns_app)
                                                        .
ra6m5_gcc_mcuboot --BL2_APP_DIR--> bl2.axf --> bl2.hex / bl2.srec
                                              (flashed raw, NEVER signed)

ra6m5_gcc_secure  ----S_APP_DIR--> tfm_s.axf --> imgtool --> tfm_s_signed.bin
                                      |
ra6m5_gcc_nonsecure --NS_APP_DIR-->   | cmake --build <spe> -- install
                                      v
                                   api_ns/
                                     +-- interface/{include,src,lib}
                                     +-- image_signing/
                                     +-- cmake/toolchain_ns_GNUARM.cmake
                                      |
                                      |  -DCONFIG_SPE_PATH=<spe>/api_ns
                                      |  -DTFM_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=.../toolchain_ns_GNUARM.cmake
                                      v
                                                        tfm_ns.axf
                                                            |
                                                            v
                                                 imgtool --> tfm_ns_signed.bin
  • The three e2 projects are inputs only. They supply the generated FSP sources, bsp_linker_info.h (the partition addresses every layout derives from) and the OFS values.
  • The slot layout comes from the secure project's Debug/bsp_linker_info.h, named above. The SPE project takes FSP_NS_APP_DIR but does not compile from it: it records the path into api_ns (<part>_ns_config.cmake) so the NS project builds against the same e2 non-secure project and can cross-check it. Those sources are compiled only under RA6M5_NS_IN_SPE_BUILD, which is off by default.
  • BL2 is not signed. It is the root of trust and is flashed raw, as .hex or .srec, never the flat .bin (D002, GETTING_STARTED.md §6). Only tfm_s and tfm_ns go through imgtool.

The invocations are in scripts/ — see scripts/README.md.

2. The library graph

Two executables in the SPE project, one in the NS project. No target below is the port's own: the port adds sources to six upstream targets (§3) and supplies the FSP module libraries (§4).

tfm_s (exe)                             secure_fw/CMakeLists.txt:57
  +-- PRIVATE  secure_fw                INTERFACE lib, :51
  |              +-- INTERFACE tfm_spm
  |              +-- INTERFACE tfm_partitions
  +-- PRIVATE  platform_s
  +-- PRIVATE  psa_interface
  +-- PRIVATE  tfm_sprt

tfm_spm                                 secure_fw/spm/CMakeLists.txt:95
  +-- PUBLIC   tfm_arch, tfm_spm_defs
  +-- PRIVATE  platform_s, tfm_boot_status, tfm_config, tfm_partitions,
               tfm_fih_headers, tfm_sprt          <-- unconditional; see §6

tfm_sprt                   secure_fw/partitions/lib/runtime/CMakeLists.txt:39
  +-- PUBLIC   psa_interface, tfm_spm_defs, tfm_config, platform_s, tfm_vprintf
  +-- PRIVATE  tfm_spm, psa_crypto_config

psa_interface (INTERFACE)               interface/CMakeLists.txt:29
  +-- INTERFACE tfm_config
      carries TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL and CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META   (:37, :40)

platform_s                              platform/CMakeLists.txt:95
  +-- PUBLIC   platform_common_interface, platform_region_defs,
  |            tfm_fih_headers, cmsis, cmsis_stack_override
  +-- PUBLIC   fsp_bsp_s, fsp_flash_s, fsp_sce_s, fsp_agt_s   <-- port, :385
  +-- PRIVATE  tfm_config, tfm_spm_defs, psa_crypto_library_config
  +-- PRIVATE  tfm_sprt    ONLY if PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ATTEST_HAL  (:109)

bl2 (exe)                               bl2/CMakeLists.txt:147
  +-- PUBLIC   bootutil                 bl2/ext/mcuboot/CMakeLists.txt:70
  |              +-- PUBLIC mcuboot_config, platform_bl2, bl2_crypto   (:30)
  +-- PUBLIC   bl2_crypto

platform_bl2
  +-- PUBLIC   fsp_bsp_bl2, fsp_flash_bl2 (+ fsp_sce_bl2)      <-- port, :696
  • bl2 does not link platform_bl2. The only route is bl2 -> bootutil -> platform_bl2, both PUBLIC. A platform symbol missing from the BL2 link is a bootutil problem, not a bl2 one.
  • Two cycles are intentional: tfm_spm <-> tfm_sprt, and platform_s <-> tfm_sprt when the attest HAL is on. CMake resolves static-library cycles by repeating archives on the link line, so these build — but they are why link trouble here has tended to be archive ordering rather than a missing library.
  • PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ATTEST_HAL is ON upstream (config/config_base.cmake:116) and OFF on both live parts (ra6m5/config.cmake:199, ra8m2/config.cmake:225) because the port supplies its own attest_hal.c. That single OFF is what makes §6 possible.

3. What the port adds to each upstream target

Targetra6m5ra8m2Sources added
platform_s387537Unconditional: target_cfg.c, tfm_hal_platform.c, tfm_peripherals_def.c, attest_hal.c, cmsis_drivers/Driver_Flash.c, sce_trng.c (PSA external RNG over the SCE9 TRNG), ra_sce_init.c, <part>_layout_checks.c (static assertions only, no code). Under CONFIG_TFM_FLIH_API OR CONFIG_TFM_SLIH_API: ext/common/tfm_hal_nvic.c (the IRQ HAL, :416) and tfm_timer0_irq.c (the AGT0 fixture handler, :425) — the privileged half of the TIMER0 fixture; plat_test.c is the other half and must stay in tfm_sprt. Separate block: Driver_USART.c when RTT is off (:682 / ra8m2 :799)
tfm_sprt453595plat_test.c, behind CONFIG_TFM_FLIH_API OR CONFIG_TFM_SLIH_API. Scoped to the one file, and given platform_s's resolved include list rather than a hand-written subset — tfm_sprt links into every partition, so the FSP tree must not reach the whole target
tfm_spm517648ext/common/tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c — the upstream file. Do not move it back to platform_s; see §6
tfm_s607724startup_<part>.c
platform_bl2704821target_cfg.c, tfm_hal_platform.c (there for one symbol: __STACK_SEAL, which anchors .msp_stack_seal_res), cmsis_drivers/Driver_Flash.c — three files, unconditional. Plus RTT or USART stdout in a later block (:747 / ra8m2 :868). Compiled with RA6M5_BUILDING_BL2 and no _RA_TZ_ macro — BL2 is a flat build. bl2_boot_hal.c is not here; see the bl2 row
bl2728843startup_<part>.c, bl2_option_setting.c — the OFS emitter, and the reason BL2 needs discrete per-word MEMORY regions in its linker script (D002). The gating differs by part. On ra6m5, if(CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR) (:735) covers both ra_sce_init.c and bl2_boot_hal.c. On ra8m2, bl2_boot_hal.c is unconditional (:854) because it enables the SAU, without which BL2 cannot read the non-secure slots; only ra_sce_init.c is behind the accelerator there (:858). Either way BL2's SHA-256 runs on the engine, and BL2 brings it up itself in boot_platform_post_init() before MCUboot hashes the first slot
tfm_ns10651204Optional path only. rtt/SEGGER_RTT.c, rtt/rtt_ns_init.c under RA6M5_STDOUT_RTT — but the whole block sits inside if(FSP_NS_APP_DIR AND RA6M5_NS_IN_SPE_BUILD) (:1021), and that option is OFF by default (:1016). See the note below

The default build has no tfm_ns target in the SPE project. RA6M5_NS_IN_SPE_BUILD (ra8m2: RA8M2_NS_IN_SPE_BUILD) exists for single-configure boot bisection and has been off by default since 2026-08-30. In the normal split build the NS image is built by the NS project — §1 and §2 — and gets its RTT from syscalls_ns.c's own _write() plus the ns_app/tests_reg sources, not from this block. rtt_stdout.c is absent by design either way: it would collide with that _write().

4. The FSP module registry

e2 studio does not emit CMake. The port turns each FSP driver into its own static library through a registry, so modules are opted into by name rather than globbed off disk, and anything in the project that no module claims is reported rather than silently dropped.

FSP_MODULES_S   = bsp flash sce agt              :234
FSP_MODULES_BL2 = bsp flash (+ sce if CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR)   :238, :242
FSP_MODULE_DIRS_bsp   = bsp r_ioport             :247
                _flash = r_flash_hp  _sce = r_sce  _agt = r_agt
          |
          v
fsp_add_modules(role, dir, includes, out_targets)         :269
          |                     called at :384 (s) and :695 (bl2)
          +-- include() cmake/modules/fsp_module_common.cmake   once
          |      add_library(fsp_<name>_<role> STATIC)      common:33
          +-- include() cmake/modules/fsp_<name>.cmake       per name
          |      -> a missing file here is a HARD configure failure
          |
          +-- glob ra/fsp/src/* ; for each directory:
                 unclaimed AND not in FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT
                   -> message(WARNING) "it is NOT in the image"      :293

the module libraries are not a flat set:

    fsp_flash_<role> --PUBLIC--+
    fsp_sce_<role>   --PUBLIC--+--> fsp_bsp_<role>
    fsp_agt_<role>   --PUBLIC--+
  • Adding a module takes three things, not two: a name in FSP_MODULES_S or _BL2, an FSP_MODULE_DIRS_<name> entry, and a cmake/modules/fsp_<name>.cmake file. See ADDING_FSP_MODULES.md.
  • The two mistakes fail differently. A name with no .cmake file aborts the configure — include() is not OPTIONAL. A missing DIRS line takes the warning path: the directory stays unclaimed and the build tells you the driver is not in the image.
  • Both roles build their own copy of a shared module, which is why the target name carries the role: fsp_bsp_s and fsp_bsp_bl2 are different libraries.
  • Every non-bsp module PUBLIC-links fsp_bsp_<role> — fsp_flash.cmake:21, fsp_sce.cmake:51, fsp_agt.cmake:40. A new module almost certainly needs the same line; ADDING_FSP_MODULES.md carries it in the template.
  • FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT (:266) is not an exclusion from the build. It is the allowlist for the audit, naming directories that are in the e2 project and are expected to be unclaimed.
    • r_sce is built, by the sce module: FSP_MODULE_DIRS_sce = r_sce (:249), and fsp_sce.cmake globs the tree. In the secure image the TRNG is always reachable; the SCE9 cipher *_ALT path is live whenever CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR is ON, which is the default (config.cmake:127). BL2 declares the module only with the accelerator, for the SHA-256 image hash. Its entry in NEVER_BUILT is therefore not redundant: it is what keeps the audit quiet in the BL2-without-accelerator case, where no listed module claims the directory.
    • rm_psa_crypto and FSP's ra/arm/mbedtls are the real omissions, as FSP modules. The *_ALT sources that drive the engine are compiled by platform/ext/accelerator/renesas/sce9 instead, and the crypto library comes from the fsp_mbedtls.cmake overlay below. FSP's crypto code is in the image; what is excluded is FSP's PSA/ITS configuration, which wires PSA ITS to littlefs and conflicts with TFM_PARTITION_INTERNAL_TRUSTED_STORAGE (DESIGN.md §6). The header of cmake/modules/fsp_sce.cmake is the authority on this split.
    • rm_mcuboot_port — its own FLASH_AREA_*_ID values and single-image assumptions conflict with TF-M's dual-image flash map (DESIGN.md §4, §5). Grafting it on is what failed on RA6M4.
  • Beside the registry, cmake/fsp_mbedtls.cmake does something larger: it FORCE-sets MBEDCRYPTO_PATH to an overlay built from the secure project's ra/arm/mbedtls. Present for ra6m5 and ra8m2 only.

5. After the link

Each is an add_custom_target(... ALL), not add_custom_command(TARGET ... POST_BUILD) — the latter only attaches to a target created in the same directory, and bl2_bin is not.

StepLineDoes what
orphan-section check837Fails on any section the linker script did not place, against a short allowlist
check_ofs.py915Reads the program headers of the linked ELF and fails if a PT_LOAD coalesces the option-setting words. Toolchain-agnostic. This is the only place the mistake is visible — not the srec, not the map, and a plausible-looking linker script is no evidence (D002, D094)
--emit-safe-bin958Re-emits the flat binary address-driven. objcopy -O binary flattens from the lowest address and zero-fills the gaps, which yields an image that can permanently lock the part
imgtool—Signs tfm_s and tfm_ns into their slots, using the layouts installed under api_ns/image_signing/. Slot overflow fails here, after a clean link

6. Why the isolation HAL's target is load-bearing

ext/common/tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c switches on six macros. Four arrive as compile definitions, and those are the ones the target choice decides. The other two arrive by header, so they are target-independent, which is why they were never part of the defect.

MacroDelivered byReaches platform_s?Reaches tfm_spm?
CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECTCMake — platform_s PUBLIC, platform/CMakeLists.txt:125yesyes
TFM_PXN_ENABLECMake — platform_s PUBLIC, platform/CMakeLists.txt:126yesyes
TFM_ISOLATION_LEVELCMake — psa_interface INTERFACE, interface/CMakeLists.txt:37noyes
CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_METACMake — psa_interface INTERFACE, interface/CMakeLists.txt:40noyes
CONFIG_TFM_MMIO_REGION_ENABLEheader — generated config_impl.hyesyes
PLATFORM_STATIC_MPU_REGIONSheader — the platform's tfm_peripherals_def.h (:268)yesyes
psa_interface  --PUBLIC--  tfm_sprt  --PRIVATE-->  tfm_spm     always
                               ^
                               |  PRIVATE, only if
                               |  PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ATTEST_HAL=ON  (OFF here)
                           platform_s
  • tfm_spm reaches the two psa_interface macros indirectly and unconditionally: it PRIVATE-links tfm_sprt, which PUBLIC-links psa_interface.
  • platform_s has no such route. Its own tfm_sprt edge exists only under PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ATTEST_HAL, which this port turns off (§2).
  • All nine upstream users of the file — an519, an524, corstone300, corstone310, mps4, musca_b1, musca_s1, rse, alcor — add it to tfm_spm. All four RA ports added it to platform_s.
  • Consequence: the file compiled with TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL undefined, so every #if on it evaluated 0. == 2 and == 3 tests were false; != 3 tests were true. The MMIO region was never programmed at isolation 2, and the partition-metadata region was never covered at isolation 3. The App RoT data arm did fire, which D120 records against an earlier "neither arm fires" reading.
  • This is a target choice, not an upstream defect. Moving the source fixed the class rather than the two macros that had been noticed. D113 through D126; the withdrawal of the upstream claim is item 15 of UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md.
